crime: Music followed {WITCH_NAME} everywhere, pouring out of the empty air. There was one girl she hushed it for. Every night, that girl stood at the upper railing and recorded one minute of the courtyard fountain on her phone.

On Sundays, at the listening hour in the lounge, she played the week's recordings, hearing them for the first time along with everyone else. One Sunday she played a fountain minute, and under the splash was {WITCH_NAME}, humming a song. The band crashed in and drowned the lounge.
At ten, {WITCH_NAME} had made a song for her father and sung it only into her sister's phone. At his memorial, her sister played it for the whole room. She had not let a room go quiet since.

That night, in the second-floor hall, the girl asked for her minute as always, and {WITCH_NAME} came up as always. This time she refused. From the far end, by the library door, she turned the band up. The girl climbed onto the lower rail and leaned out over the courtyard to catch the fountain under the music. She slipped over as her phone clattered onto the hall floor. As she fell, the band broke into a crash, then silence.
{WITCH_NAME} went to the railing, sobbing into the quiet. The phone lay there, still recording her. She stamped it to pieces.

Down in the courtyard, the prisoners had heard the band pour over the railing as if it were right beside the girl, then a crash like a struggle, and the girl fell dead onto the path. They ran up and found {WITCH_NAME} alone at the railing, the phone smashed under her heel. In the trial court, they ruled that she had pushed the girl and smashed the recording.
No hand had touched the girl. She fell reaching on her own, and the one record that showed it was the phone {WITCH_NAME} broke.
fields.epitaph: The only sound that could have saved her was her own, in the quiet.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Never Let a Room Go Quiet
execution: In the trial court, the execution stand raises two great bronze cymbals on iron arms. She is chained upright between them. The cymbals clash on her from both sides, again and again, ringing out the crash her band made at the railing. Then they part and hang still. She hangs slack in the chains as the ringing fades to silence.

magic.name: Live from Nowhere
magic.text: She can fill any room she's in with the music in her head, as if an unseen band were playing.
